A small first experiment

The context experiment

Ask the same model to choose a meeting room with six versions of the input. Check whether it gets the right answer—and whether it had the facts it needed.

What you’re testing

Two teams share a folder of room options and requirements. A useful rule for one team can distract from the other team’s task.

Read the study design
Use a model running on your computer. Each trial starts with a fresh input.

What do the six policies mean? +
Full
All eight blocks, in the original order.
Full, grouped
The same blocks, arranged by the team they apply to.
Recent
Only the last few blocks in the packet.
Lexical
Blocks selected by word overlap with the question.
Scope-aware
Blocks for the target team and shared information.
Oracle
The four blocks we know are needed. A diagnostic, not a realistic selector.
“Facts included” measures coverage of four annotated evidence blocks. “Other team’s answer” counts answers that match the other target’s solution; it cannot establish why a model chose them. Oracle trials are skipped below a four-block budget.


What to try next
The result should help us choose between improving selection, making rules clearer, or revisiting the task itself.


Look at each input and answer +
Each trial will include the exact input, answer, and scoring decision.


How much can we conclude? +
This is a small synthetic pilot. It tests one decision per call, not a complete agent workflow. Source-block budgets are not token budgets, and a handful of trials cannot establish which policy is generally better.
Use it to find cases worth investigating. The paired tasks share documents, so they are not statistically independent. Partial runs are not balanced comparisons. Nothing is saved automatically: download your results before closing this page.
